selection_criteria: The 80 most recently published GitHub-reviewed advisories for the pip ecosystem as of 2026-08-07, capped at 2 per source repository and 1 per fixing commit, restricted to those carrying a CWE and a fixing-commit reference into their own repository whose parent is not a merge, whose fix diff is under 400 KB, and which touch reviewable Python source outside tests and docs. Ground-truth spans are the lines the fix removed, excluding spans that are entirely imports, version bumps or comments. Two fixing commits were then excluded by hand as bulk refactors whose spans mark remediation plumbing rather than the defect; the reasons are in benchmark/corpus/labelled-excluded.txt. NOT filtered by CWE: classes no 3a detector can emit are retained and reported as a stratum. Newest-first sampling makes the set post-cutoff for any model evaluated later.

advisory.summary: LangGraph: Namespace prefix matching crosses segment boundaries in Postgres and SQLite stores

findings.title: Namespace prefix search drops segment-boundary and LIKE-escaping

evidence.why: search() now builds `store.prefix LIKE '<prefix>%'` from raw _namespace_to_text with no segment anchor and no escaping of `%`/`_`, so a prefix ("foo",) also matches ("foobar",) and a label containing `%`/`_` acts as a wildcard, matching unrelated namespaces (the removed _namespace_prefix_condition/_escape_like_literal and their tests enforced exactly this isolation).

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: list_namespaces prefix/suffix match uses unescaped, unanchored LIKE

evidence.why: prefix/suffix match_conditions now build `prefix LIKE '<path>%'` / `LIKE '%<path>'` with only `*`→`%` substitution; metacharacters in a path segment are not escaped and the segment-boundary regex is gone, so suffix ["alice"] also matches "malice" and `%`/`_` in a segment silently become wildcards.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: SQLite search namespace_prefix condition loses segment-boundary/escaping and case-sensitivity

evidence.why: `s.prefix LIKE ?` / `prefix LIKE ?` is built from raw _namespace_to_text with no escaping and no boundary anchor, so ("foo",) matches ("foobar",), labels with `%`/`_` act as wildcards, and LIKE's ASCII case-insensitivity (unlike the removed GLOB-based condition) conflates namespaces that get/put/delete treat as distinct.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: SQLite list_namespaces prefix/suffix match drops segment-aware/escaped matching

evidence.why: The NS_MATCH_FUNCTION regex path (segment-anchored, metacharacter-escaped) is replaced by plain `prefix LIKE ?` with only `*`→`%` substitution, so suffix ["alice"] now also matches "malice" and labels containing `%`/`_` are treated as wildcards instead of literal text.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

AIOHTTP: HTTP request smuggling via WebSocket upgrade

findings.title: Upgrade requests no longer drain their request body before switching protocols

evidence.why: This reverts the fix in CHANGES/13016.bugfix.rst: `_upgraded` is now set immediately when an Upgrade header is present, and the body-reading branch is skipped whenever `self._upgraded` is true regardless of Content-Length/chunked framing, so a request with an Upgrade header and a body is treated as having no payload. If the upgrade is subsequently rejected by the application, the unread body bytes remain on the wire and get parsed as the start of the next request/response, enabling request smuggling across a shared connection (the removed test test_declined_websocket_upgrade_reads_body demonstrated exactly this scenario).

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: C parser skips body parsing for any Upgrade/CONNECT request instead of deferring the switch

evidence.why: cb_on_headers_complete now returns 2 (no body, upgrade now) as soon as an Upgrade header or CONNECT method is seen, rather than deferring the protocol switch until after the body is consumed via the removed `_pending_upgrade` state machine; a request with a body and an Upgrade/CONNECT that is ultimately not upgraded will leave its body unread on the connection, causing the next parse to desynchronize with subsequent bytes (smuggling).

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

advisory.summary: AIOHTTP: HTTP request smuggling via WebSocket upgrade

advisory.summary: proot-distro has a Container Isolation Bypass via Crafted Restore Archive

findings.title: Hardlink source no longer restricted to the restoring container

evidence.why: The check `link_container != restore_name` was removed; only `link_src is None` is checked now. Since restore now tracks multiple containers via `pending_locks`, a crafted archive member can set `linkname` to a path in a different (possibly pre-existing, unrelated) container and have `os.link`/copy read from that container's rootfs into the archived container, letting one container's restore read arbitrary files out of another container on the host.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Restore no longer rejects archives naming multiple containers

evidence.why: The explicit rejection of a second container name (`elif container_name != restore_name: ... sys.exit(1)`) was removed and replaced with per-container lock/clear tracking (`pending_locks`, `cleared`), so a single restore invocation now silently clears and overwrites every container named in the archive instead of failing closed on an archive that doesn't match the single-container backups the tool itself produces, widening the blast radius of a tampered or hostile archive.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

advisory.summary: proot-distro has a Container Isolation Bypass via Crafted Restore Archive
`proot-distro install` has a Symlink Escape (Arbitrary Host File Write) via Malicious Tar Archive

findings.title: Removed symlink-clamped path resolution re-opens tar extraction traversal

evidence.why: _process_member now builds parent/dest with plain os.path.join(rootfs_dir, *rel_parts) instead of _safe_resolve; a crafted archive can plant a symlink (e.g. evil -> /) followed by a member evil/passwd and the write follows the symlink outside rootfs_dir, since only '..'/'' components in the member name are filtered, not pre-existing symlinks in the destination tree.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Deferred hard-link copy no longer clamps src/dest through symlinks

evidence.why: extract_tar_to_rootfs now copies deferred_links using raw (dest, src) paths computed at defer time without re-resolving via _safe_resolve; a later or earlier member's symlink can redirect either endpoint outside rootfs_dir, letting shutil.copy2 read a host file or write outside the container.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Directory creation no longer removes a same-named symlink before os.makedirs

evidence.why: The removed `if os.path.islink(dest): _remove_fstree(dest)` check meant a planted symlink occupying a directory member's name is no longer cleared, so os.makedirs/os.chmod can act through the symlink onto its target.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: restore command drops symlink-clamped dest/link-source resolution

evidence.why: command_restore no longer calls the removed _safe_dest before writing dest or resolving link_src for hardlinks; a crafted backup archive with a symlink member followed by an entry under it can write through the symlink onto the host filesystem, and hardlink members can copy an out-of-rootfs file via a linkname routed through a planted symlink.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: _materialise_files writes through unresolved symlinks in rootfs_dir

evidence.why: host path is now built with plain os.path.join(rootfs_dir, arcname.lstrip('/')) instead of _safe_resolve, so a file_map entry whose parent directory was previously materialised as a symlink (e.g. from an ADD'd tar) can redirect the write outside rootfs_dir.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

advisory.summary: `proot-distro install` has a Symlink Escape (Arbitrary Host File Write) via Malicious Tar Archive

datamodel-code-generator vulnerable to arbitrary local file read via JSON-Schema `$ref` (`file://` and `../` traversal), bypassing `--no-allow-remote-refs`

findings.title: Local $ref path traversal / arbitrary file read no longer restricted to base path

evidence.why: The removed _resolve_local_ref_path check that rejected or warned on local $ref targets resolving outside self.base_path has been deleted; _get_ref_body_from_remote now does `full_path = self.base_path / resolved_ref` and _get_ref_body_from_url just does `file_path = Path(path)` for file:// refs, so a schema with a relative ($ref: "../../../etc/passwd") or absolute/file:// ref is loaded and its contents inlined into generated output with no containment check, even under --no-allow-remote-refs, since that flag now only gates HTTP(S) targets.

findings.title: file:// refs now bypass --no-allow-remote-refs entirely

evidence.why: The new condition `if not resolved_ref.startswith("file://") and self.http_local_ref_path is None:` skips the allow_remote_refs=False error path whenever the ref uses file://, so an attacker-supplied schema can reference arbitrary local files via file:// URIs even when the operator explicitly disabled remote/external ref fetching.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

advisory.summary: datamodel-code-generator vulnerable to arbitrary local file read via JSON-Schema `$ref` (`file://` and `../` traversal), bypassing `--no-allow-remote-refs`

findings.title: Local $ref outside base path allowed by default with only a warning

evidence.why: _resolve_local_ref_path only raises when allow_remote_refs is explicitly False; when unset (None, the default) a local $ref that resolves outside base_path is still followed after emitting a deprecation warning, so an untrusted schema can read arbitrary local files unless the caller passes --no-allow-remote-refs.

advisory.summary: pytonapi has a Webhook Custom Path Authentication Bypass

findings.title: Custom webhook paths no longer get their own token, silently disabling auth

evidence.why: setup() now only ensures a webhook for the default suffix path (self._path + suffix) instead of iterating every distinct registered path; handlers registered with a custom path= (via account_tx/_make_decorator) never get an entry in self._tokens for that path, so process() has no expected token to check against requests on that path. The removed test test_setup_enforces_auth_on_custom_path explicitly verified this was previously enforced.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: _build_path_map collapses multiple registered paths per event type

evidence.why: The rewritten _build_path_map keeps only handlers[0][2] (the first-registered path) per event type instead of mapping every registered path to its event type, so incoming webhook requests on any additional/custom path registered for that event type can no longer be resolved/authenticated correctly by process().

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

libp2p: yamux connection DoS via oversized data frame

findings.title: Removal of oversized-DATA-frame guard and read timeout enables resource exhaustion / DoS

evidence.why: The diff removes both the check rejecting DATA frames with length > MAX_WINDOW_SIZE and the trio.fail_after timeout wrapping the body read (_read_data_body), replacing bounded reads with plain read_exactly. A peer can announce an arbitrarily large length with SYN/ACK/normal DATA frames and either withhold the body indefinitely (hanging handle_incoming forever, since read_exactly will block awaiting bytes that never arrive) or force allocation/processing of a huge buffer, with no timeout or size cap to tear down the connection.

findings.title: Server now fails open when read-only operations index fails to load

evidence.why: main() previously re-raised on index load failure to refuse startup; now it logs a warning and sets READ_OPERATIONS_INDEX to None, allowing the server to start and requests to proceed under a fallback policy instead of failing closed.

findings.title: Weakened fallback policy when security index is unavailable

evidence.why: When READ_OPERATIONS_INDEX is None, the denylist/elicit-list enforcement (check_security_policy) is entirely bypassed for the process lifetime; only READ_OPERATIONS_ONLY_MODE and REQUIRE_MUTATION_CONSENT gate execution, meaning denylisted operations can execute unchecked if the index fails to load and read-only mode is off.
